claim.pdf_says: In the 14.9.48.2 UNSTRING general format the ON OVERFLOW group is drawn as a tall BRACKET with a plain full-height VERTICAL BAR immediately inside each side (verified on a 300 dpi crop: the outer glyph has square bracket serifs top and bottom, the inner glyph is a bare vertical rule with no serifs): "[| ON OVERFLOW imperative-statement-1 |]" over "[| NOT ON OVERFLOW imperative-statement-2 |]" as one two-row enclosure.
claim.markdown_says:
```
⌐ ⌐                                        ¬ ¬
| |  ON OVERFLOW imperative-statement-1     | |
| | NOT ON OVERFLOW imperative-statement-2  | |
L L                                        ⌐ ⌐
```  (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 32385-32390)
claim.why_it_matters: The inner enclosure is drawn with corner glyphs (⌐ top, L bottom) on both the outer AND the inner element, so the figure reads as two NESTED BRACKETS rather than a bracket carrying choice indicators. Per 5.2.6.4 a bracket pair enclosing stacked alternatives means AT MOST ONE of them, whereas a bracket with choice-indicator bars means zero or more, each at most once, in any order. As transcribed the figure says an UNSTRING statement may carry ON OVERFLOW or NOT ON OVERFLOW but never both - falsely restrictive, the exact defect class already confirmed on GOBACK, CALL Format 2, STRING, START, SEND and RECEIVE. The sibling STRING statement (14.9.43.2, line 31964) renders the identical construct correctly as ⌈ | ... | ⌉ plus an explanatory figure note, so this is transcription drift, not a convention.

verdict.reasoning:
INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED by rendering page 799 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v799/spec_p799.png) and re-cropping the ON OVERFLOW enclosure at 6x (crop_left.png / crop_right.png).

WHAT THE PRINTED GLYPHS ACTUALLY ARE. Left side: two distinct rules. The OUTER (leftmost) glyph is a square bracket '[' - a vertical stroke with a short horizontal serif at its TOP and another at its BOTTOM, both projecting rightward. The INNER glyph, immediately to its right, is a BARE vertical rule: a single unbroken stroke, taller than the bracket, with NO serif at either end. Right side mirrors it: a BARE full-height vertical rule with no serifs, then the closing ']' bracket whose serifs project leftward. That is unambiguously the printed form '[ | ... | ]' - one bracket pair carrying a pair of choice-indicator bars - not two nested bracket pairs. Two nested brackets would show FOUR serif corners per side (eight total); the page shows exactly two per side (four total), all on the outer glyph.

WHAT THE MARKDOWN ACTUALLY SAYS. Verified byte-exact with `sed | cat -A`. The transcription convention in this very file draws a single bracket pair as corner glyphs on the first and last rows and '|' on the interior rows - see the DELIMITED BY figure eight lines above (specs/ISO_COBOL.md 32378-32381): '⌐ ... ¬' / '| ... |' / 'L ... ⌐'. The ON OVERFLOW block DOUBLES every corner glyph: '⌐ ⌐ ... ¬ ¬' on the top row and 'L L ... ⌐ ⌐' on the bottom row. Under the file's own convention that is TWO NESTED BRACKET PAIRS, because a choice-indicator bar carries no corner glyph on the corner rows. The distinction is not theoretical: the sibling STRING figure at 31969-31970 renders the identical printed construct correctly as '⎡ | ON OVERFLOW ... | ⎤' / '⎣ | NOT ON OVERFLOW ... | ⎦' - corner glyph, then bare bar - and carries an explicit figure note citing 5.2.6.4. So the file distinguishes the two forms elsewhere and got UNSTRING wrong.

THE MEANING CHANGES, AND NORMATIVELY. 5.2.6.4 (line 2701): 'Choice indicators are a pair of bars, |, that enclose a portion of a general format. ... When enclosed by brackets, zero or more of the alternatives contained within the choice indicators shall be specified, but any single alternative may be specified only once. ... The alternatives may be specified in any order.' A plain bracket pair around stacked alternatives (5.2.6.2/5.2.6.3 semantics) admits at most one. So the transcription forbids writing both phrases on one UNSTRING; the printed page permits both, in either order.

CORROBORATED BY THE PAGE'S OWN GENERAL RULES, which are transcribed correctly. GR 16 e) (line 32513) reads 'The NOT ON OVERFLOW phrase, if specified, is ignored' - stated inside the overflow branch, i.e. in a statement that ALSO specified ON OVERFLOW (GR 16 c/d). GR 17 (line 32515) likewise says the ON OVERFLOW phrase 'if specified, is ignored and control is transferred to the end of the UNSTRING statement or, if the NOT ON OVERFLOW phrase is specified, to imperative-statement-2.' Both rules are only meaningful if a single UNSTRING may carry BOTH phrases - which the nested-bracket transcription prohibits. The transcribed figure therefore contradicts the transcribed normative rules on the same page.

I attempted every available refutation and none holds: the glyphs are not a rendering artifact (visible at 6x with clean serif/no-serif contrast); it is not reflow or page-break furniture (the figure is wholly on page 799); the claim does not misquote either source (PDF crop and `cat -A` both match); and it is not a house convention (the STRING sibling proves the file's convention is the opposite).
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, and described accurately in substance. One citation correction: the fenced block is at specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 32388-32393 (fence 32388, corner rows 32389 and 32392, text rows 32390-32391), not 32385-32390 as claimed - lines 32385-32386 are the '[ WITH POINTER identifier-7 ]' and '[ TALLYING IN identifier-8 ]' lines. The defect itself: page 799 prints the UNSTRING ON OVERFLOW / NOT ON OVERFLOW group as a single bracket pair enclosing a pair of choice-indicator bars ('[ | ... | ]'; outer glyph has top and bottom serifs, inner glyph is a bare serif-less vertical rule, confirmed at 6x on both sides), which per 5.2.6.4 means zero or more of the two phrases, each at most once, in any order. The markdown doubles the corner glyphs on both the top and bottom rows ('⌐ ⌐ ... ¬ ¬' / 'L L ... ⌐ ⌐'), producing two nested bracket pairs, which under 5.2.6.2/5.2.6.3 admits at most ONE of the two phrases. This falsely forbids 'UNSTRING ... ON OVERFLOW ... NOT ON OVERFLOW ... END-UNSTRING', a form the page's own General rules 16 e) and 17 presuppose is legal. FIX: render the block as '⎡ | ON OVERFLOW imperative-statement-1 | ⎤' / '⎣ | NOT ON OVERFLOW imperative-statement-2 | ⎦' and add the same 5.2.6.4 figure note the sibling STRING statement carries at line 31974, which UNSTRING currently lacks entirely. Same defect class as the already-confirmed GOBACK, CALL Format 2, STRING, START, SEND and RECEIVE findings.
